extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical Euclidean-style geometry (historic Italian mathematical readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and geometric/arithmetic methods for constructing, comparing, and computing lengths, areas, and solids in classical (Euclidean-style) geometry; includes constructions with similar triangles, perpendiculars, squares, and proportional arithmetic manipulations for extracting roots and areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use similar triangles to equate products of segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Products and ratios of line segments can be related by forming similar triangles; multiplication of one pair of segments equals the multiplication of the corresponding pair when the triangles are similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly uses the fact that if triangles are similar (angoli formali e triangoli simili), then corresponding sides are proportional, so one may infer equal products (la multiplicatione ... iguale). It demonstrates combining multiplications obtained from different similar triangles to conclude equality of products and to derive lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Square-on-side and root extraction via geometric squares
rubrics_metrics.description: To find squares and square roots of lengths/numbers, form geometric squares on segments (quadrato del diametro, quadrato della parte) and use area relations to deduce roots; squaring and taking square roots is accomplished by multiplying/dividing by appropriate factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript shows procedures to form the square of a diameter or cathetus and to use those areas to obtain roots of compound numbers (le radici, la radice di uno cenfo ...). It also prescribes multiplying by powers of 10 (100, 1000, 10000) to convert numbers into perfect squares before extracting roots (multiply each part in fe etc.). Examples and arithmetic adjustments are given to handle non-square quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute lengths by arithmetic scaling (multiply/divide by powers of ten)
rubrics_metrics.description: When numerical lengths are not perfect squares, multiply parts by powers of 10 (100, 1000, 10000, etc.) to make them convenient for geometric operations, then divide back to recover the original scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several worked examples instruct multiplying each part by 100, 1000, 10000 (uno cenfo, uno cenfo e.10000) so that the square roots become integral or easier to manage; after geometric operations, scale back by dividing by the same factor. The text gives iterative examples showing this technique for computing roots and areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a point equidistant from given vertices (circumcenter) by perpendicular bisectors
rubrics_metrics.description: A point equidistant from the vertices (cime) of a polygon or the vertices of a triangle is obtained by constructing lines equidistant from the given points (perpendicular bisectors) and taking their intersection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage on 'equidistante dalle cime' prescribes constructing loci equidistant from given vertices and obtaining the desired point by intersection of equidistant lines/constructs. The method involves dropping perpendiculars and constructing equal segments so that the selected point has equal distances to the specified vertices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pythagorean relation for right triangles (squares on sides)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a right triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the two legs; this relation is used to compute lengths and to relate areas (la quadratura della ipotenuzza ... le due parti).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats right triangles and shows that squares on sides combine to form the square on the diameter/hypotenuse (potumilTa / ipotenuzza), using this as a basis for many constructions and numeric manipulations: forming squares on legs, adding them, and relating to the square on the hypotenuse to deduce unknown lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find centers and special points by intersecting constructed lines (perpendiculars, medians, bisectors)
rubrics_metrics.description: To locate special centers (center of triangle, center of face, etc.), construct appropriate perpendiculars, medians, or bisectors from known vertices or diameters and take their intersection as the desired center point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show finding the center of a triangle (centro del ... triangolo) by constructing line segments (catetto, diametro) and using perpendiculars or bisectors to determine the point equidistant from vertices or faces. The text prescribes stepwise geometric operations to locate such centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare volumes/solids of pyramids by base area and height proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Volumes (or the solidities) of pyramids are compared and related by proportions of their bases and heights: pyramids having proportional base areas and corresponding heights have volumes in the same proportion (le piramidi fanno fra lojo ippo ... per le loro altezza e medelima base).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript gives procedures for embedding smaller pyramids into larger ones, scaling by multiplying base areas and heights (taking diameters of bases, etc.), and using multiplicative arithmetic to compute the resulting 'solidity' of pyramids. It also prescribes operations to combine and compare the solidities via proportional arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct (or 'square') a figure: form a square equal in area to a given figure by decomposition and recomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: To construct a square equal in area to another figure (triangular face, combined areas), decompose the figure into parts, perform proportional multiplications, and recombine to obtain a square with area equal to the original figure (fare il quadrato della magnitudine etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text walks through decomposing triangles and other plane regions, multiplying parts, and assembling the resulting areas to make an equal square. Instructions include forming double of differences and combining quadratures to reach an equal-area square (la quadratura, partire nel doppio della differanzia...). Examples illustrate how to convert non-square areas into a square via algebraic-geometric operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct equilateral triangles and regular polygons by repeated equal-side constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: An equilateral triangle and other regular polygons (e.g., a regular pentagon as discussed) are constructed by reproducing equal sides and transferring lengths around a circumferenced figure; the center-to-vertex distances and central angles are equal in regular polygons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections labelled on 'triangolo equilatero' and on pentagons explain that in an equilateral triangle all faces and central distances are equal, and give methods to build regular polygons by taking a side, using it to construct adjacent equal sides, and ensuring equal central angles. The guidance includes forming the necessary perpendiculars and equal-length transfers to create the polygon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use perpendiculars and parallels to produce loci equidistant from lines/points
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce lines or points equidistant from given lines or points, draw the necessary perpendiculars or parallels and use their intersections to identify the locus satisfying the equidistance condition (equidiltante, equidistant lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript frequently prescribes drawing parallels and perpendiculars (perpendicolari, parallele) from specified points and using repeated equal arcs or segments so that constructed points are equidistant from given sources (e.g., along sides of triangles or from circle centers); procedural steps and numeric examples illustrate these constructions.
